mechanism_narrative: Declining RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks (-13.3% to -17.9%) represents a persistent downward trend that will continue into the next four weeks absent a reversal signal. Momentum in negative direction persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -13.3% to -17.9% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (8.1% to 9.6% over four weeks) signals increased essential-goods shopping trips. Consumers consolidating errands will substitute retail-and-recreation visits with grocery-focused trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC further.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM sustains above 9.0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point in weeks where GROCERY_PHARM remains above 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed (-22.4% at t-0w), indicating weak commuting and reduced urban circulation. This suppressed transit use constrains retail foot traffic because retail clusters depend on transit-enabled access. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as long as TRANSIT stays below -20%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while TRANSIT remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from 26.1% (t-2w) to 4.6% (t-0w), signaling a shift away from outdoor recreation. This reallocation of leisure time will redirect consumers toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, reversing the RETAIL_REC decline if PARKS drop persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 8% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from 26.1% to 4.6% over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -15% when PARKS mobility is below 8% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -8.6% to -10.6%, indicating partial remote-work adoption. When combined with sustained RESIDENTIAL elevation (3.4% to 4.0%), this signals home-centric behavior that suppresses retail visits. The interaction of low workplace and elevated residential mobility will keep RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -8% AND RESIDENTIAL above 3.5% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -8.6% and RESIDENTIAL at 4.0% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points when WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL maintain the observed pattern for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT decline of -22.4% indicates possible mobility restrictions or transit service reductions. If this policy-driven transit suppression persists, retail-and-recreation venues dependent on transit access will experience continued foot-traffic losses, keeping RETAIL_REC negative.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% within four weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: March 15 marks early spring in Northern Hemisphere. Seasonal shift toward outdoor activity (PARKS at 4.6% but historically volatile) combined with improving weather will gradually redirect consumers from indoor retail to outdoor recreation, further suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS volatility from 4.6% to 26.1% suggests seasonal sensitivity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points when PARKS mobility rises above 15% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of sustained GROCERY_PHARM strength (9.6%) and collapsed PARKS mobility (4.6%) indicates consumers are prioritizing essential errands and avoiding discretionary outdoor activity. This behavioral shift will suppress RETAIL_REC as discretionary shopping remains depressed when essential shopping is elevated and outdoor alternatives are weak.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 9.0% AND PARKS below 10% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 9.6% and PARKS at 4.6% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% when GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 9.0% and PARKS remains below 10% for two consecutive weeks.
